notes.title: Alpha 9 - Sandbox Editor (+Contest)
notes.content:
Alpha 9 is out now! Another important step taken :-) Here is what it adds to the early access version of Imagine Earth:

[h1]Sandbox Galaxy[/h1]
As introduced in the last Friday Report, you are now able to generate as many planets as you like to and save them to the Sandbox Galaxy. You can use each of them for the Free Play and Time Trial mode (described below).
http://youtu.be/RN-fUT7S-FE

[h1]Editor[/h1]
Since generating planets clearly isn't enough we added the editor. The editor works for all of your sandbox planets. You can start it in the planet menu - the same place you would start a Free Play. Within the editor you can terraform (Keyboard M and N), define the type of every field and place and remove every building you like. Finally save the result and go back to the Sandbox Galaxy to play your planet. Watch the video to see everything in detail.

[h1]Time Trial mode[/h1]
After raising the limit with new Landing Permissions and Research Tokens for up to 20 million people on each planet, we decided to include a first draft of the Time Trial mode.

This mode is made up of up to 5 race goals like "500,000 people until week 500". If you reach one goal the race for the next starts. If you fail one goal, you loose. The time you have for each goal depends on the amount of population needed and the difficulty you choose.

The Time Trial mode is clearly not perfect yet. We look forward to hear your feedback.

[h1]Trade with Natives[/h1]
[url=http://www.imagineearth.info/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/2015-03-05_NativesTrade.jpg][img]http://www.imagineearth.info/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/2015-03-05_NativesTrade-780x439.jpg[/img][/url]

The natives on Rounos will now sell their precious and tasty food to you. Make sure to negotiate first, because otherwise they wont trade with you. The food price depends on their mood and the maximum amount on the number of forests surrounding them.

Natives added to a sandbox map will also trade with you.

[h1]Details[/h1]
Two details among other things we changed:
[list]
	[*]Your operation systems setting for left handed mouse control is detected and used. Did you know that there are 10-15 % of left handeds folks amoung us?! ;)[/*]
	[*]Your population now grows based on the space available. This means you will have to deal with the problem of supplying enough resources. The population growth is based on the level of difficulty so you can still keep it easy if you want.[/*]
[/list]

[h1]What didn't make it?[/h1]
[list]
	[*]Mission Bora, because we put our focus on the Sandbox Galaxy and Editor for this release.[/*]
	[*]The Warehouse, because we are still not sure whether it should be able to store all three resources or just one of them at a time.[/*]
[/list]

[h1]What is guessed for Alpha 10?[/h1]
[list]
	[*]The final mission on Bora![/*]
	[*]Volcanoes[/*]
	[*]Steam Workshops for sharing Sandbox planets[/*]
	[*]Steam Achievements and Trading Cards[/*]
	[*]A new game mode with AI opponents[/*]
[/list]

[h1]Early Access Contest - 3 Steam keys to be won[/h1]
Win a Steam key for a friend by populating Joma Free Play with the most people. One important condition: You have to maintain a positive climate balance. Upload your Steam Screenshots to our community board on steam. The winners are announced in next weeks Friday Report #3 in the blog section!

notes.title: Friday Report #2
notes.content:
We plan to update the early access version with Alpha 9 next Friday. The glorious final campaign mission and the AI we are working on will not be part of this release. But there will be a lot of other new features that will be fun and worth a try.

So let's keep this short and go with some more screenshots.

[h1]What did we do the last 7 days?[/h1]
[list]
	[*]The [b]AI now considers the influences[/b] that buildings have on each other. This way they make much betters choices on what building to take and where to place it.[/*]
	[*]We completed the basic [b]trading system[/b]. You can read more about it in last weeks post and see a screenshot of it in the header.[/*]
	[*]Destroyed [b]City Centers can now always be rebuilt[/b]. This is because we realized that it really s*cks to rebuild your whole city in a new location when your City Center has been destroyed by a twister or something else (and you didn't unlock the rebuild tool from the research).
[url=http://www.imagineearth.info/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2015/02/2015-02-26_RebuildCityCenter.jpg][img]http://www.imagineearth.info/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2015/02/2015-02-26_RebuildCityCenter-780x439.jpg[/img][/url][/*]
	[*][b]Sandbox Galaxy[/b]: This one is my weeks favorite! You can create a new planet and it is saved to the sandbox galaxy so you can (re)play it anytime. This is the foundation to integrate Steam Workshops for planet sharing into the game (YEAH!).
[url=http://www.imagineearth.info/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2015/02/2015-02-26_SandboxGalaxy.jpg][img]http://www.imagineearth.info/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2015/02/2015-02-26_SandboxGalaxy-780x439.jpg[/img][/url][/*]
	[*]The [b]free game mode[/b] now will give you coins and new city centers until you reach [b]20 mio[/b] people.[/*]
	[*]Currently the population stops to grow when you are out of resources. Thanks to the feedback of one dear follower (thanks Bora!) we realized that it's much more interesting to let the [b]population grow based on the space available[/b]. This means you will have to deal with the problem of supplying enough resources. The population growth is based on the level of difficulty so you can still keep it easy if you want.[/*]
	[*]The [b]Warehouse[/b] is a new building type that will have some deeper influence on the gameplay. You can use it to store overproduced resources. If your population grows too fast or some buildings are destroyed the resources from your warehouse are used to meet the demands of your people. The screenshot shows a small bar over the goods balance representing the total amount of stored goods. In the top left you can see the absolute amount for the focused warehouse.
[url=http://www.imagineearth.info/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2015/02/2015-02-26_Warehouse.jpg][img]http://www.imagineearth.info/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2015/02/2015-02-26_Warehouse-780x439.jpg[/img][/url][/*]
	[*][b]Crash the server[/b]: Ok, this one was really stupid. I (Martin) decided to have a short try updating some libraries on our server and ended up crashing the whole thing at 2am. Not the best way to finish your day I can tell you. Luckily it's working again thanks to the backup made by our hosting. Thanks a lot for this feature.[/*]
[/list]

[h1]What's planned for next week?[/h1]
Main focus is still on the Bora mission and maybe we will add the volcanoes that didn't make it last week. But since the next Alpha version is due Friday 6th of March, we will focus on things that can be used within the release. For instance the natives on Rounos will start to trade their special food with you and we hope to add a first version of the sandbox editor so you can terraform your generated planets.

[h1]Anything else?[/h1]
Nope. We have to get back to work now. There are things to be done. You know.

notes.title: Friday Report #1
notes.content:
[b]What is happening behind the scenes?[/b]

We learned that some of you would like to follow our work in more detail. This post is a first try to give you some insight into our weekly development.

[h1]What did you accomplish during the last 7 days?[/h1]
[b]Jens:[/b]
Hey Guys. One of various things that I did this week was creating the concept and design for a planetary trade system that looks pretty promising.

Next I made a first draft for some new characters (see post title):
The space merchant will come around when you have some valuable gems and products to offer to trade them for research tokens and more... The Electronic Employer is the ultimate planet exhauster. Major Eko is good for sub-quests regarding environmental issues. The Illuminati are the natives of Bora. Living in their pyramids they got a very strange technology to turn the planets forces against you if you turn out not being a friendly visitor.

Additionally to these new characters I made a design concept video for how the communication with these guys might look much more sci-fi style in the future. It's on our new youtube channel and you really should set the quality to high.

http://youtu.be/vagEfZPP-yQ

[b]Martin:[/b]
First thing I have been working on is an [b]artificial intelligence[/b] for computer players that will be used in the Bora mission. Right now it simply starts to grow it's population by building districts. Resource buildings are built whenever required. Some parts are still missing though. The AI still has to learn that building a lot of fisheries next to each other doesn't make sense. In addition it only grows it's city to level 2 for now.

Next I have started to implement the [b]trading system[/b] we have been discussing lately. It will allow you to buy resources from natives and to trade with friendly AI players.

[url=http://www.imagineearth.info/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2015/02/2015-02-20_Trading.jpg][img]http://www.imagineearth.info/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2015/02/2015-02-20_Trading-780x439.jpg[/img][/url]

In between I added the new characters and temple buildings for the Illuminati to the game.

The last thing (some minutes ago) was implementing the [b]Warehouse[/b] that stores overproduced goods so they can be used for bad times (see the bar over the goods balance at the top center of the screenshot).

[h1]What will you do this week?[/h1]
Our main focus will be adding all gameplay elements necessary for the [b]Bora mission[/b]. There might be some volcanos, additional AI routines and other stuff like that. If there is some free time available we will create a [b]galaxy screen[/b] for your sandbox planets. This screen will allow you to "discover" new planets which means that you will be able [b]to keep the generated planets[/b] and collect them on a screen similar to the one from the campaign. One day (or hopefully already in some weeks) we will also add the ability to terraform those planets and to add and remove all available buildings so you can create interesting scenarios like demolished cities.

[h1]Anything else?[/h1]
The AI we are building for the computer players on Bora is only a first step. We want to make this available for the free play, too. But obviously it will take some more time to make sure the computer becomes a good player and opponent.

[b]We hope this was somehow enlightening for you.
If so please leave a short "great" in the comments.[/b]

notes.title: Update: Development Menu and Production Bonus
notes.content:
It’s only two weeks after our last update, but we added some new features to Imagine Earth and decided to release them before Christmas.

[img=http://www.imagineearth.info/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/2014-12-19_DevPanel.jpg]

So here is what’s new:
[olist]
[*]Statistic on the air pollution of all your buildings
[*]Enhanced visualization of building influences. Outgoing influences are displayed, too now (e.g. the influence of a Forestry on a Factory). Furthermore we decided to leave decimal values away to make the information more clear.
[*]Sound volume: You can now control the volume of music and sounds in the game.
[*]Production bonus: In real life a diversified resource production is more stable than relying on a single resource (like mono-culture). To take this into account you receive a resource bonus when at least two building types each produce 10% or more of a resource.
[*]Development menu: This has already been mentioned and now made it’s way into the game. You can use it to develop new buildings and upgrades. It makes it more easy to compare the different building types and understand the relationships between them. In addition it is still possible to develop buildings and upgrades in the build and tool ring.
[/olist]

The video gives a short introduction on the development menu,  production bonus and the influences some buildings have on each other:

http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rkIfXjBojrA

The next update is planned for end of January.

Your thoughts and feedback are welcome!

notes.title: Rounos Reworked
notes.content:
Hi, we have just published a new early access version on Steam. It brings a completely reworked Rounos mission. The old script had too much stuff happening in parallel. We changed this and it's much more straightforward now. Special events and side-quests are better communicated and highlighted on the planet and in the mission briefing.

A side effect is that old Rounos savegames wont work anymore. Sorry for that, but there were too fundamental changes to the mission.

Your thoughts and feedback about the reworked Rounos mission are welcome! 

[h1]Terraforming Preview[/h1]
We are currently experimenting with procedural planets and terraforming. [url=www.imagineearth.info/terraforming-sandbox-preview]Read more about it on our blog.[/url]

notes.title: Steam Leaderboards Integrated
notes.content:
Hey, we have just integrated Steam Leaderboards into the Imagine Earth score system. After an update on Steam you can see your score for every planet and compare to …

[list]
[*]steam friends
[*]people in your country
[*]people around the globe.
[/list]

Please note that you will have to finish a mission again to upload the score to Steam.

Tip: If you are using multiple Imagine Earth profiles (e.g. sharing the game with a friend or relative) the best score will count. So you can have kind of a local competition between profiles and only the best will put his or her score to the global leaderboards.

In addition to the leaderboards we also made the Joma mission a bit easier and added new graphics for every planet.

Your thoughts and feedback about the new leaderboards are welcome!

notes.title: Update 0.7.5
notes.content:
Imagine Earth received a new interface look, resource statistics, a rework of Tuto with new buildings and more. Welcome to our latest Imagine Earth update on Steam - only a month after our last update. Here are the details of everything it will bring to you.

[url=http://www.imagineearth.info/steam-update-released-0_7_5]Read a cleanly formatted version with pictures on our blog.[/url]

[olist]
[*]Difficulty levels easy, normal and hard. They adjust the consumption of your cities and the pollution of all buildings. This will make a huge difference in terms of how easy it is to populate you planets with huge colonies.
[*]The new interface look is much cleaner and comes with some new icons and an improved Info panel in the bottom left.
[*]New character art!
[*]New resource statistics can be opened by clicking into the resource panel at the top.
[*]Cattle breeding and Biomass power plant are two new buildings. In addition Jens added new graphics for a lot of the other buildings.
[*]Tuto got completely reworked and will now start with more buildings and real choices. In addition we slightly adjusted the goals and story in Joma. This means that savegames of both missions wont work anymore and will be hidden and you can replay both missions to get the stars for the new goals.
[*]The campaign screen now displays all unlocked planets within a galaxy and visualizes their different magnitude.
[*]Planet rotation is now locked so north stay always on top. A small change that makes a huge difference - it's now a lot easier to keep the orientation on your planet!
[*]Using the build menu now immediately places the building. You can still choose a different placement field by keeping the button pressed.
[*]Balancing & Bugs - as always.
[/olist]

Spooktacular Halloween Wishes!
Jens & Martin

PS: We didn't manage to add configuration options to the free play mode. The reason is that we are still working on the final concept for free play in Imagine Earth.

PS²: An update of the demo will follow next week. 

PS³: [url=http://www.imagineearth.info/blog]You can follow our weekly devlog[/url]

[img=http://www.imagineearth.info/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2014/10/2014-10-31_Release_0_7_5.jpg]

notes.title: Update: Planet Rounos and much more
notes.content:
It took much too long, but now it’s done. We have uploaded version 0.7.0 of Imagine Earth to Steam some minutes ago and hope you have a lot of fun with it! 

[url=http://www.imagineearth.info/steam-update-released]Read a cleanly formatted version with pictures on our blog.[/url]

This is what’s new:
[olist]
  [*]Planet #4 “Rounos” with the next mission of the campaign
[list][*]AI building a competing colony[/list]
  [*]City names (as promised in the crowdfunding)
  [*]New buildings:
[list]
  [*]Solar park
  [*]Financial district
  [*]Watchtower
  [*]Mine
  [*]Forestry
[/list]
  [*]New world elements
[list]
  [*]Crystals
  [*]Boss ship
  [*]Native camp
[/list]
  [*]Enhanced research system
  [*]New tools
[list]
  [*]Disable buildings (to save resources)
  [*]Relocate buildings
[/list]
  [*]Wildfires 
  [*]Riots (within native camps)
  [*]Gui enhancements
[list]
  [*]Options within main menu
  [*]New savegame menu (number of savegames is no longer limited)
  [*]Highlight player regions in navigation mode
[/list]
  [*]#RL: Founded a company (previously we have been a partnership)
[/olist]

[b]Time to play Imagine Earth now ;-)[/b]

Jens & Martin

PS: [url=http://www.imagineearth.info/blog]You can follow our weekly devlog[/url]

[img]http://www.imagineearth.info/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2014/09/2014-09-30-Rounos.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Early Access Now
notes.content:
We are really excited to let you know that we have just published the early access version of Imagine Earth on steam – just in time.

Here is the list of the new features:

[list]
[*]Episode II: Lorian. This is one monster of a mission. Featuring a 4 times bigger planet than Joma was, with enough space for multiple cities and several million people.
[*]New research system: Fulfilled mission goals are rewarded with stars that can be used to unlock new tools and technologies.
[*]Meteorite strikes – beautiful until they hit you.
[*]New buildings and world elements: Mountains, Research District, Nuclear Power Plant, Oil Platform, Fishery, Buoy Station, Organic Farm and Recycling Factory.
[*]Loads of small gameplay changes and balancing.
[*]New graphic style – we decided to replace the outlines with dynamic shadows and more atmospheric day and night lighting.
[*]Free Play mode for Tuto, Joma and Lorian.
[/list]

We hope you have a lot of fun with this version and would love to hear your feedback and see screenshots (press F12) of the best and worst situations you experience. So please post in the steam community or join our forum at http://forum.imaginearth.info.

Jens & Martin
